search_row.title: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
search_row.statement: The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.
search_row.math: u(p) = \frac{1-e^{-4N_e s p}}{1-e^{-4N_e s}}; neutral limit u(p) = p, so a new mutant fixes with probability 1/(2N)

fields.dct:source: Motoo Kimura (1962) On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Track the fate of many marked mutations of measured fitness effect in replicate experimental populations of known N_e (e.g. barcoded microbial lineages) and compare fixation frequencies with u(p).
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: diffusion approximation to the Wright-Fisher model, genic (additive) selection with coefficient s, constant effective size N_e, no linkage to other selected sites. Formal status: proved within the diffusion limit.
